ozet: In the Data Forest, Piko organizes the hero's bag with a list: making a list, adding, removing and changing items, and exploring it with sum, max and sorted.

giris.anlatim: Day 5: Lists! In this lesson you'll organize the hero's bag with a list: adding items, removing them, and exploring the list.

cikis.anlatim: The interactive version of this lesson is waiting for you at 30gunde.com.tr. Write your code right in the browser, run it instantly, and finish the tasks!
maddeler: Write and run code in your browser
Learn Python step by step in 30 days

sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! Welcome to the Data Forest. Every hero on an adventure carries a bag: a sword, a potion, a map. Keeping dozens of items in separate variables would be hard. The solution? A list!
A list is values separated by commas inside square brackets. append adds a new item to the end. Just like with strings, indexes start at zero, and len tells you how many items there are.

ekran.kod:
inventory = ["sword", "potion"]
inventory.append("map")
print(inventory)
print("First item:", inventory[0])
print("Item count:", len(inventory))

sahneler.anlatim: remove throws the first matching stone out of the bag. With in you ask whether an item is there. pop removes the last item and hands it back to you, so you can catch it in a variable.

ekran.kod:
inventory = ["sword", "potion", "stone"]
inventory.remove("stone")
print(inventory)
print("potion" in inventory)
last = inventory.pop()
print("Removed:", last, "Left:", inventory)

sahneler.anlatim: To change an item, write its position number and put in the new value. insert adds at any position you like; say zero, and it goes to the very front.
For lists of numbers, sum gives the total, max the biggest and min the smallest. sorted returns a new sorted list and leaves the original alone. Slicing works just like with strings.

ekran.kod:
scores = [40, 85, 60, 95]
print(sum(scores), max(scores), min(scores))
print(sorted(scores))
print(scores[0:2])

sahneler.anlatim: A list with three items has no item number three! Counting starts at zero, so the last item is number two. Python says IndexError: that position is outside the list. For the last item, minus one is always safe.

ekran.cikti: IndexError: list index out of range

sahneler.anlatim: Take a guess! Which two numbers does this code print?
Four and five! append added five to the end, so the list has four items. And minus one gave the last item, which is five.
